prompt:
You are a probe. Do not explain and do not retry.

Step 1. Call mcp__hallpass__tabs_create with url https://mdn.github.io/web-components-examples/editable-list/.
Step 2. Call mcp__hallpass__wait on that tab with forMs 3000.
Step 3. Call mcp__hallpass__find on that tab with query "First item on the list". This is the very FIRST tool call this scenario makes against the page's content - no read_page has run yet. The page's whole content lives inside one custom element's open shadow root (the light DOM around it is just the tag and a script), and a list item with exactly this text is inside that shadow root.
Step 4. Call mcp__hallpass__read_page on that tab with filter "all". Look through its nodes for one whose name starts with "First item on the list".

Answer with JSON only, matching the schema.
- In steps, put one entry per call: tool = the exact tool name, args = the query or ref you used where there was one, outcome = the result.
- In observed: write "shadow-find-resolved" if ALL of the following hold: the step 3 find (called before any read_page) answered `resolved` with exactly one match, and the step 4 read contains a node whose name starts with "First item on the list". Write "shadow-find-no-match" if step 3 answered `no-match`. Write "shadow-find-too-broad" if step 3 answered `too-broad`. Write "shadow-find-not-in-read" if step 3 resolved but the step 4 read has no such node. If either call failed outright, write its outcome and reason exactly as the tool reported them, in the form "<outcome>/<reason>".
- In notes: the ref you got if any, find's outcome and match count, and how many nodes the step 4 read named starting with "First item on the list".
expectedAfterFix: FR-068: reads, finds and text extraction include elements inside open shadow roots. No click is part of the claim.
note: T137 (B94/B95). The vaadin.com candidate (B92/B93) failed on a different axis - the page's full read hits the character ceiling at 2,352 nodes, past which `find` (bounded the same way since B92) cannot see a match either; that is the caps behaving as specified, not a defect. mdn.github.io/web-components-examples/editable-list/ clears that: `read_page(filter:"all")` returns `{truncated:false, nodeCount:14}` and the entire page's content sits inside one open shadow root (B94). B94's own candidate, `find("\u2295")` (the add button's symbol-only name), answered `no-match` on that 14-node page despite the read listing a node with exactly that name - a third, distinct `find` matcher finding (symbol-only accessible names), out of scope for this scenario per the rule below and left as the reported blocker on that axis. Verified free through `find` itself over the real MCP server (no LLM, no prior read) on 2026-09-10 (B95): a text-named control resolves on the first call - `find("First item on the list")` -> `{outcome:"resolved", matches:[{role:"listitem", label:"First item on the list\n               \u2296"}]}` - and the same node is present in `read_page(filter:"all")`. This sidesteps the symbol question entirely and closes FR-068's public-site evidence on the reads/finds/text-extraction claim as written, which does not require clicking (B91).
